# Decisions: initiative-supersession

- 2026-09-11T06:21:55.624Z — rule: **Supersession is recorded ONLY as `successor` on the predecessor's superseded status event — never written on the successor, never inferred from prose; every reverse view derives from that one field.** — chose **Supersession is a THIRD closed status, `superseded`, on the existing initiative_status_changed event, carrying `successor: <slug>` — recorded ONCE on the old record and derived everywhere else. The successor's side (`supersedes: a, b` in the listing, the reverse edge in the graph and reach index) is computed at read time from the predecessors' status events; nothing is written on the new record. `sofar new --supersedes` is sugar: create, bind, then one ordinary superseded close per predecessor.** over (1) A merge command that copies events into a third record via the cursor primitive — rejected: envelope.initiative inside every copied line would name the old slug (the misroute signature fold.ts and record-integrity 2.1 warn about), task ids collide across records, plan_updated is whole-plan so the ulid-newest wins, and renumbering to fix any of that is a rewrite the append-only log forbids. (2) A new event type `initiative_superseded` — rejected: superseded IS a closed status, and every reader that already asks isClosedInitiativeStatus (list, next, doctor, banner, statusline, end-session) gets it for free, where a new type would need each of them taught separately. (3) Writing `supersedes: [a, b]` on the successor's initiative_created too — rejected: two records asserting one edge can disagree, and the record already derives the reverse of a fact rather than storing both halves (commit-attribution D1). because The user-reported gap (initiative-lifecycle note, 2026-09-10) was never that events could not be copied — the hand-built workaround copied the plan fine. It was that closing 'pointing at' the successor left NO edge: a bare slug in a note is not a citation (citations.ts binds a slug only as the qualifier before a handle), so status, find and the banner all lost the pointer. One field on the event the close already appends is the smallest thing that turns that prose into an edge, and putting it on the OLD record matches where the fact lives — the old record is the one that stopped, and it is the one a session lands on by mistake.
